uncited: *   **Input:** Primary ray hit point $\mathbf{p}$, area light source geometry (defined by a set of sample points), and volume data structure.
**Generate Shadow Ray Packet:** For a given primary ray hit point $\mathbf{p}$, generate $N$ shadow rays.
**Traverse Volume:** Traverse the volume data structure along each ray $\mathbf{r}_i$ in the packet.
*   **Number of shadow rays ($N$):** Controls the quality of the penumbra approximation.
*   **Light source size:** The spatial distribution of sample points $\mathbf{l}_i$ defines the effective size of the area light.
*   **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot K)$, where $N$ is the number of shadow rays per packet and $K$ is the number of volume samples traversed per ray.
*   **Memory Complexity:** $O(N)$ for storing the ray packet directions and intermediate transmittance values.
It leverages the inherent coherence of ray packets to make soft shadow computation feasible in real-time or near-real-time volume rendering applications.
